# Legion Intelligence

> Legion Intelligence builds governed agentic AI for national security. Legion deploys AI agents that carry out work across the systems teams already use: humans command, agents operate, and every action is attributed. Legion is delivered through Legion Packs, role-based capability bundles that put agents to work on day one, and extends to disconnected tactical environments through Centurion by Legion Intelligence. Legion runs in cloud, on-prem, air-gapped, classified (IL2 through IL6), and edge environments.

**Legion Intelligence** is the company's full name. This document refers to it as **Legion** after first mention. Legion turns human intent into coordinated, governed action: humans define objectives, constraints, and priorities; AI agents carry out the work across systems and data; governance enforces policy, provides full attribution, and keeps humans in command at every step.

Legion is built for national security: the U.S. Department of War (DoW), the intelligence community, the U.S. Department of Energy, and public-sector-adjacent organizations. The same capability and governance extend to critical infrastructure and adjacent industries, including aerospace, manufacturing, maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO), energy, and pharmaceutical production.

Tagline: **Command with Confidence**

---

## Product Hierarchy

Three names cover everything Legion ships:

- **Legion** is the secure, governed foundation that connects agents, models, data, and existing systems under human authority. Everything Legion ships runs on it.
- **Legion Packs** are role-based capability bundles and the way Legion is purchased and used. Each Pack contains the agents, workflows, data connections, and governance required to perform a specific job.
- **Centurion by Legion Intelligence** is Legion's deployable edge AI system for DDIL environments: hardware, software, and sustainment in one purchase. Same Packs, same governance, connected or disconnected.

---

## Legion Packs

Legion Packs are role-based AI capability bundles that deliver outcomes out of the box. Most AI tools start with a prompt box; mission teams need software built for the work they actually do. Each Pack deploys a ready Space with the Apps a team needs to start work immediately. No prompt engineering, no blank chat box, no months of integration.

Four Featured Packs are available today:

- **Commander Pack**: Helps leaders see what needs a decision, what has changed, and what actions are already underway. Users: commanders, senior enlisted advisors, executive officers, battle captains.
- **Intelligence Officer Pack**: Turns scattered reporting and operational data into faster intelligence products, threat context, and decision support. Users: J2/S2 intelligence officers, intelligence managers, intel staff.
- **Operations Officer Pack**: Enables operations teams to plan, coordinate, track, and update activity without manually rebuilding context every shift. Users: S3/J3 operations officers and staff sections.
- **Maintenance Technician Pack**: Helps maintenance teams search technical manuals, create and schedule work orders, check parts, and reduce repair delays that affect readiness. Users: maintenance technicians, field techs, maintenance supervisors. Apps include Inspection WO Generator, Work Order Scheduler, Manual Assistant, Parts Manager, and Parts Kit Builder.

Packs start ready and extend without starting over. Custom Apps are built into a Pack in weeks for use cases unique to a mission, and new Packs deploy as new roles and operational needs emerge.

Learn more: https://www.legionintel.com/mission-packs

---

## Centurion by Legion Intelligence

Centurion by Legion Intelligence is a deployable edge AI system integrating hardware, software, and sustainment for DDIL (denied, degraded, intermittent, limited connectivity) environments. Centurion runs the same Legion Packs, the same Pack/Space/App architecture, and the same governance as cloud and on-prem deployments, from a single node to a coordinated mesh. Cloud connectivity is an accelerator when available, never a requirement for operation.

Model routing is automatic. When connected, Centurion routes to the latest customer-approved frontier models. When degraded or disconnected, it shifts to the latest locally hosted open-weight models, with no operator intervention. Workflows and governance are preserved in both states, and updated models are deployed to edge nodes with controlled rollout, so the edge never becomes a frozen, outdated AI island.

Four deployment models (May 2026):

- **Centurion III** (1 user): Intel-based laptop built on Intel AI PC technology with Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors. For forward operators and small teams that need local AI without constant connectivity.
- **Centurion V** (up to 2 users): NVIDIA DGX Spark. Backpack-portable for small-team mobile deployment and forward operational bases.
- **Centurion X** (up to 50 users): HPE Edgeline EL8000 with NVIDIA GPU. Vehicle-mounted or forward operating base use, with rugged case options tested to MIL-STD-810G and MIL-STD-461 and TAA-compliant configurations available.
- **Centurion L** (up to 350 users): HPE ProLiant DL380a Gen12 with multi-NVIDIA GPU. For FOB datacenters, embassies, and air-gapped networks.

Procurement is a single purchase: hardware, software, models, and support in one line item, with a known BOM, fixed pricing, and HBOM/SBOM documentation ready for accreditation. Solution delivery and ecosystem partners include Intel, HPE, Rancher Government Solutions, Google, and NVIDIA.

Learn more: https://www.legionintel.com/centurion

---

## How Legion Works

Customers interact with four things: Packs, Spaces, Apps, and Collections.

- A **Pack** is a role-based bundle that deploys a ready working environment with the tools a specific role needs.
- A **Space** is a structured working environment where teams organize and carry out their work. Spaces define who has access, what context is available, and how work is coordinated.
- An **App** is an AI-powered tool designed to complete a specific task from start to finish. Examples: SITREP Generator, Award Writer, Manual Assistant, Work Order Scheduler.
- A **Collection** is the governed knowledge layer that powers every result with permissions and provenance.

Across every Pack and App, Legion agents:

- **Search**: Agentic search across an organization's entire document ecosystem. Agents query by topic, keyword, or content, surface what is relevant, and trace every result back to source, governed by existing access policies.
- **Chat**: Answers in plain language from an organization's own data. Agents pull context from across systems and file types and cite their sources.
- **Create**: Drafts of emails, reports, and proposals grounded in organizational data. Every claim traces back to source, and humans review before anything ships.
- **Automate**: No-code agentic workflows that carry multi-step work across systems end to end, with humans approving the steps that matter and full auditability.

Underneath, Legion connects to 100+ systems (including IBM Maximo, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, ServiceNow, Jira, and Box), supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP), offers REST API extensibility, and runs any model: open-source, proprietary, or fine-tuned. New models are added through the Model hub without code changes.

## Why Choose Legion

- **Velocity**: Compress the distance between intent and action. Packs deploy ready capability on day one, and custom Apps ship in weeks, not quarters.
- **Resiliency**: Built for the environments missions actually run in. Cloud, on-prem, air-gapped, classified, edge. Any model, no vendor lock-in.
- **Control**: Humans command. Agents do the work. Governance across data, models, agents, and permissions, with full attribution and auditability.

---

## Security and Deployment

Legion is FedRAMP High authorized, NIST 800-53 compliant, SOC 2 Type II certified, and CMMC Level 1, is ready to manage ITAR-controlled data, and is authorized for deployment from IL2 through IL6, including air-gapped networks. HIPAA and GDPR attestations are in place. HBOM/SBOM documentation supports accreditation.

Data sovereignty is enforced by design: customer data stays in the customer's environment and is never used to train models. Role-based access controls, approval workflows, guardrails, and audit logging govern every action, including agent actions, with full attribution showing what was done and on whose behalf.

Deployment options: cloud, on-prem, hybrid, air-gapped, and edge (through Centurion).

Learn more: https://www.legionintel.com/security

## Proven Results

- 48x faster INTSUM generation and 15x faster target system analysis (Scarlet Dragon 26-01, XVIII Airborne Corps G2, on tactical SIPR at IL6)
- 94% faster intelligence summary generation (Targeting Officer, U.S. Special Operations Command)
- 216 hours saved per week automating repetitive manual workflows (Battalion Staff, U.S. Special Operations Command)
- 88% reduction in SITREP processing time (8 hours to under 1 hour)
- 25% increase in technician capacity (Manual Assistant, Amentum)
- 1-day field install to operational capability, with most users proficient within one hour (Scarlet Dragon 26-01)
- USSOCOM TE 26-02: Centurion ran Military Decision Making Process (MDMP) workflows on government-provided planning data in a disconnected environment, shifting automatically to locally hosted models when network access was unavailable
- A U.S. Department of Energy national laboratory: 95% reduction in code development time (one week to a half day) and 6.5+ hours saved per task, generating documented, explained code for research validation over CUI and sensitive proprietary data
- A U.S. Department of Energy national laboratory: source verification 12x faster (about two hours to minutes) and 80% less follow-on research, using RAG-grounded workflows that return real, cited research papers, scaling from 25 users toward 500

The same platform proven by 20,000+ users across U.S. Special Operations Command.

## Who Legion Is For

Legion serves national security organizations: defense, the intelligence community, DOE, and public-sector-adjacent teams. Functional leaders (commanders, J1 through J4 directors, deputy chiefs of staff) deploy Legion to increase operational tempo, maintain readiness, and field AI under human authority in classified and edge conditions.

The same requirements extend to critical infrastructure: electric utilities, oil and gas, pharmaceutical production, and other regulated manufacturing, where a compromised or failed system can cause physical harm. These operators face the constraints Legion was built for: sensitive data that cannot leave the environment, operations that cannot depend on cloud connectivity, and AI that must stay governed, auditable, and under human authority.

Industries with dedicated pages today:

- [Defense](https://www.legionintel.com/industries/defense): Governed AI for every mission function, from intelligence to logistics
- [Aerospace](https://www.legionintel.com/industries/aerospace): Sustain readiness across maintenance, parts, and supply workflows
- [Manufacturing](https://www.legionintel.com/industries/manufacturing): Connect ERP, MES, supply chain, and maintenance systems
- [MRO](https://www.legionintel.com/industries/maintenance-repair-operations): Diagnose faster, cut return trips, and keep equipment ready

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What is Legion Intelligence?**
A: Legion Intelligence is a governed agentic AI company for national security. Legion deploys AI agents that carry out work across the systems teams already use, delivered through role-based Legion Packs. Humans command, agents operate, and every action is attributed. Legion runs in cloud, on-prem, air-gapped, classified (IL2 through IL6), and edge environments.

**Q: What are Legion Packs?**
A: Legion Packs are role-based AI capability bundles. Each Pack contains the agents, workflows, data connections, and governance required to perform a specific job. Customers deploy a Pack aligned to a role (Commander, Intelligence Officer, Operations Officer, Maintenance Technician) and start work immediately in a ready Space with the right Apps.

**Q: Is Legion Intelligence a chatbot?**
A: No. Chat assistants answer questions; Legion Packs carry out work. Each Pack ships with Apps that connect to existing systems, complete multi-step jobs under human approval, and produce outcomes such as intelligence summaries, work orders, and reports. The job is the unit of value, not the conversation.

**Q: What is Centurion by Legion Intelligence?**
A: Centurion by Legion Intelligence is a deployable edge AI system integrating hardware, software, and sustainment for DDIL environments. It runs the same Legion Packs and governance as cloud and on-prem deployments, connected or disconnected, from a single node to a coordinated mesh, with automatic failover to locally hosted models.

**Q: What is the difference between Legion Intelligence and Centurion?**
A: Legion Intelligence is the company and the governed system its agents run on. Centurion is Legion deployed as a portable, edge-native form factor for disconnected and degraded environments. Centurion runs the same Packs, the same Pack/Space/App architecture, and the same governance as every other Legion deployment.

**Q: What does DDIL mean?**
A: DDIL stands for denied, degraded, intermittent, and limited connectivity. DDIL describes operating environments where network access cannot be assumed. Centurion by Legion Intelligence is built for DDIL conditions: it runs Legion Packs on locally hosted models with no cloud dependency and synchronizes when connectivity returns and policy permits.

**Q: Can Legion Intelligence run in classified or air-gapped environments?**
A: Yes. Legion Intelligence is authorized from IL2 through IL6 and deploys in cloud, on-prem, hybrid, air-gapped, and edge environments. The same Packs run identically across all of them, including fully disconnected deployments through Centurion by Legion Intelligence.

**Q: Is Legion Intelligence FedRAMP authorized?**
A: Yes. Legion Intelligence is FedRAMP High authorized. Legion is also NIST 800-53 compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified, is ready to manage ITAR-controlled data, and is authorized for IL2 through IL6 deployments, with HBOM/SBOM documentation established for accreditation.

**Q: What security certifications does Legion Intelligence hold?**
A: Legion Intelligence holds FedRAMP High authorization, SOC 2 Type II certification, and NIST 800-53 compliance, is ready to manage ITAR-controlled data, and is authorized for IL2 through IL6 deployments including air-gapped networks. HIPAA and GDPR attestations are in place. HBOM/SBOM documentation supports accreditation.

**Q: What AI models does Legion Intelligence support?**
A: Legion Intelligence is model-agnostic and runs open-source, proprietary, and fine-tuned models. Connected deployments route to the latest customer-approved frontier models; disconnected deployments run the latest locally hosted open-weight models. New models are added through the Model hub without code changes, so deployments stay current as models release.

**Q: Does Legion Intelligence train on customer data?**
A: No. Customer data stays in the customer's environment and is never used to train models. Mission data never leaves your environment. With customer-approved cloud models, only the minimal data required to fulfill a request is sent; fully local deployments keep all processing inside the environment.

**Q: How does Legion Intelligence preserve human authority?**
A: Legion Intelligence runs every step under human direction or approval, based on policy the organization sets. Full attribution shows who did what, when, and on whose behalf, including for agent actions. Role-based permissions govern data, models, and agents, and audit logs are built in, not bolted on.

**Q: What systems does Legion Intelligence integrate with?**
A: Legion Intelligence connects to 100+ systems, including IBM Maximo, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, ServiceNow, Jira, and Box, and supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP). REST API extensibility allows connection to legacy and custom systems, so Legion layers onto existing infrastructure without migration or replacement.

**Q: How quickly can Legion Intelligence deploy?**
A: Legion Intelligence deploys in weeks, not months. Packs arrive with ready capability aligned to the role on day one, and custom Apps are added in weeks as needs emerge. At the edge, Centurion installed in a single day at Scarlet Dragon 26-01, with most users proficient within one hour.

**Q: How is Legion Intelligence different from building a custom solution?**
A: A custom build starts from scratch and each environment becomes a separate build. Legion Packs start with outcomes already wired into Apps and Spaces, and the same foundation runs beneath every Pack, so capability transfers across cloud, on-prem, air-gapped, and edge environments and adapts without re-architecture.

**Q: Who uses Legion Intelligence?**
A: Legion Intelligence is deployed across the U.S. Department of War and the U.S. Department of Energy. Named customers include the U.S. Army (XVIII Airborne Corps), the U.S. Air Force, the Missile Defense Agency, and the Defense Industrial Base. The same platform proven by 20,000+ users across U.S. Special Operations Command.

**Q: What is the Legion Intelligence platform?**
A: The Legion Intelligence platform is the secure, governed foundation beneath Legion Packs and Centurion. It connects agents, models, data, and existing systems, and provides the controls every deployment inherits: role-based access, approval workflows, guardrails, audit logging, and full attribution. Customers experience it through Packs, Spaces, Apps, and Collections.

**Q: What is the difference between Yurts and Legion Intelligence?**
A: Legion Intelligence is the company formerly known as Yurts. The rebrand reflects the company's focus on national security: agents that carry out operational work under human command, deployed in the classified, air-gapped, and edge environments where missions actually run.

**Q: What AI models does Legion Intelligence support?**
A: Legion Intelligence is model-agnostic and runs open-source, proprietary, and fine-tuned models. Connected deployments route to the latest customer-approved frontier models; disconnected deployments run the latest locally hosted open-weight models. New models are added through the Model hub without code changes, so deployments stay current as models release. If a model's approval status changes, teams switch models without re-architecting; no Legion deployment depends on a single model vendor.
